cells.tense: You are reading the structure underneath the thing you are aiming at, and it is sharpening the aim.
cells.ask: Name the structure you've already spotted. Then take the next step you were planning on taking.
cells.core:
You can see the pattern under the thing you want. Not a distraction from it — the reason the pursuit holds. What you strip away sharpens what you act on, and the direction stays yours.

Read right, this is leverage. You have the shape of the problem, so you know where to press. The reading and the moving are one motion: you pick a step because you understand the structure, and it gets clearer because you took the step. Put a name on what you've seen, then take the step. Nothing is waiting for you to finish understanding before it lets you move.
cells.sheetLine: You see the pattern and it points the way.
cells.verb: stripping the surface away until only the pattern remains
cells.place: in the push toward a stated goal

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of this goal that has not arrived, and the analysis is tightening around a future you cannot yet write.
cells.ask: Write down every conclusion you already have. Then leave one alone for a week.
cells.core:
You are reading the pattern harder than the goal requires. Every layer peeled back reveals another, and the pile of analysis is now what you are carrying — not the goal. Action keeps getting deferred until the structure is clear enough.

Read right, the mapping serves the aim, and you stop once you have enough to move. The bend is that you don't stop. Structure doesn't clear before you move; it clears by moving, and you have enough of the shape already. The piece you're hunting for is not hidden. It is in the way. Let one conclusion sit unexplained for a week, and see whether the goal is still there when you stop holding it up.
cells.sheetLine: You are analyzing the goal instead of moving toward it.
cells.verb: stripping the surface away until only the pattern remains
cells.place: in the push toward a stated goal

cells.tense: You are standing at a door you stopped opening, and the direction you move in is the one directly in front of you.
cells.ask: Take one thing you have been taking literally, and write what else it might be pointing at.
cells.core:
You stopped looking under the surface. The effect is quiet and ongoing: you take things as given now. The plan is the plan. The problem is the problem. No pattern asks to be seen, so none is seen, and you move in the direction directly in front of you.

Read right, this looks smaller than it sounds. You ask what one familiar thing might be, and the answer changes how you handle it. A habit turns into a signal. A plan turns into a preference. You don't need depth everywhere — you need it in one place you have been walking past. The door is not far. It is the next thing you decide to look at twice.
cells.sheetLine: You take things at face value and the depth is waiting.

cells.tense: The pattern is running underneath the goal you are already moving toward, but you describe it as just the way things are done.
cells.ask: Name one pattern in how you work toward what you want. Say aloud that it is yours.
cells.core:
You have already seen the structure. It shows in how you work — the steps you take, the order you take them in, the parts you skip. You call it the process or the job, as though it existed without you.

The pattern is yours. It was not imposed by the goal or the work. Read right, you can say what shape you gave it and change your mind about part of it. That recognition hasn't caught up to the doing yet. Once it does, the pattern becomes something you can adjust, rather than something that runs on its own while you call it the work.
cells.sheetLine: You built the pattern you credit to the work.
